chunks: Have they other associates who have prescribed another law for them which has not been dispensed by God? But for the decisive Word (of God) a sentence would have been passed amongst them. Surely there is a grievous punishment for the ungodly.

key_terms.شُرَكَاءُ: Associates or partners (of God, i.e., false deities)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about false deities prescribing their own laws?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the contrast between divine revelation and human innovation (bid'ah), particularly emphasizing the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in interpreting the Deen. The phrase 'Kalimat al-Fasl' (the decisive word) is often interpreted as God's promise of delay in final retribution, allowing time for repentance, while also pointing to the ultimate judgment where truth will be clearly distinguished from falsehood. It serves as a reminder that any religious legislation not rooted in divine command is ultimately invalid.
